page: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 48-core, 96-thread Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, supported by an expansive 480 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 192.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 5,700 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, with zero included public IPv4 addresses and no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reflect exceptional parallelism and data throughput. The c8id.24xlarge scores in the top tier (top 10%) on Geekbench multi-core (22,327.0), PassMark CPU (106,825.4), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (655.64 GB/sec). Hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions drives top-tier performance in extended instructions (133,724.65) and PassMark encryption (108,061.71). It also achieves top-tier throughput in software compilation via Clang (70,004.0) and ray tracing (120,624.0), alongside strong memory bandwidth reaching 362.34 GB/sec on uncached reads.

The 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio represents an efficient density model for CPU-intensive infrastructure, maximizing parallel throughput per resource unit. High-throughput local NVMe storage combined with strong memory bus performance makes it well suited for distributed build systems, large-scale CI/CD pipelines, high-concurrency batch compute, real-time compression services, and temporary low-latency caching architectures like Redis.
